children: Panama's comptroller general said on Wednesday it had filed a criminal complaint over suspected irregularities uncovered in an audit of a state contract with a unit of Hong Kong conglomerate CK Hutchison
The comptroller's office said the complaint seeks an investigation into possible crimes linked to the port concession contract between the state and the CK Hutchison unit, Panama Ports Company (PPC).
It said the filing covers former board members of the Panama Maritime Authority between 2014 and 2023, former administrators of the authority during that period, and PPC itself.
The authority and PPC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The complaint stems from findings in an audit of the company's financial statements and compliance with contractual obligations, the comptroller said.
The office did not detail the suspected irregularities, but said it had turned over documentation to the public prosecutor for investigation.
The move marks the latest development in a broader dispute over PPC's role operating the Balboa and Cristobal ports near the Panama Canal, one of the world's busiest maritime waterways.
Earlier this year, Panama moved to unwind the company's port concessions, escalating a legal and diplomatic fight involving PPC and CK Hutchison.
PPC has also accused Panamanian authorities in recent months of unlawfully seizing property and documents during the takeover of the facilities, allegations President Jose Raul Mulino has rejected.
The dispute has complicated CK Hutchison's proposed sale of a majority stake in its global ports business to a consortium led by BlackRock and Mediterranean Shipping Company.
